title: Public participation at board meetings
summary: How to speak during public comment, and how the board responds.
body: Speakers sign up before the meeting starts and have three minutes. The board does not respond during public comment; the superintendent follows up in writing within ten school days.

title: Public records requests
summary: How to request district records, and how long a response takes.
body: Requests go to the communications office. The district acknowledges a request within three business days and states when records will be available (story timelines).

title: Website accessibility
summary: District websites and documents meet WCAG 2.1 AA, and anyone can report a barrier.
body: The district's websites, documents and videos are designed to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA. Board meeting recordings are captioned. Report a barrier to the accessibility coordinator, who responds within five school days.

title: Superintendent evaluation
summary: The annual evaluation process for the superintendent.
body: The board evaluates the superintendent each September against goals adopted the previous year.

title: Food allergies
summary: How schools plan for students with food allergies, and how menus list allergens.
body: Under review: first reading October 20, 2026. Menus list the major allergens in each main dish. Families of students with allergies complete a care plan with the school nurse.

title: Student transportation
summary: Who rides the bus, how stops are set, and walk zones.
body: Students who live more than one mile (elementary) or one and a half miles (secondary) from school are eligible to ride. Stops are reviewed every October.

title: Student attendance
summary: Excused and unexcused absences, and when schools call home.
body: Revised October 20, 2026. The first two days of a family emergency are excused. Schools call home after the second unexplained absence in a month.

title: Student conduct and discipline
summary: Expectations, restorative practices and the steps before any suspension.
body: Schools use restorative conversations first. Families are told the same day about any removal from class.

title: Staff conduct and communication with students
summary: How staff communicate with students and families, including on approved platforms.
body: Staff use district accounts and approved platforms to contact students and families.

title: Grading and reporting
summary: How grades are reported to families, and how often.
body: Under review: first reading November 3, 2026. The draft moves to standards-based report cards in grades K–5 and posts middle and high school grades at least every two weeks.
